liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Bertha** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls the Bertha, Greatest Story and Cold Rain & Snow opening one of the best versions, setting high energy; Reviewer praises a strong Bertha and Greatest Story opening, with energy sustained through the first set [30][31]
- **Deal** (1 review): Reviewer calls the Deal closing the first set smokin' [31]
- **Ship Of Fools** (1 review): Reviewer says Ship of Fools set a tranquil mood after the second-set opening of Touch of Gray into Man Smart [30]
- **Morning Dew** (1 other source): Uploader had not heard a Dew all year and went to Buffalo for it, getting a great one [1]
- **U.S.Blues** (1 review): Reviewer describes U.S. Blues as very bouncy [30]

## The recordings

- **gd1989-07-04.118538.aud-matrix.pzm-dak5245.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 156 min [1]
- **gd1989-07-04.akg414s.alexander.78771.flac16**: source not stated; 23 songs; 158 min; rated 4.25/5 by 8 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds this audience recording acceptable, but wishes a soundboard were available [21]
- **gd1989-07-04.akg414s.alexander.78959.flac24**: source not stated; 23 songs; 157 min [3]
- **gd1989-07-04.166433.mtx.tobin.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 160 min [9]
- **gd89-07-04.aud.wiley.9045.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 21 songs; 161 min; rated 4.45/5 by 33 [10]. Said about its sound: Reviewer considers this the better of the two audience sources then on the archive; Reviewer says levels on the recording are unremarkable [23][26]

## Around the show

- Reviewer recalls Rich Stadium as a choice eastern venue and mentions a 4-21-2009 show there with N2O vendors [24]
- Reviewer watched five or six fireworks shows from the top row of the stadium during the U.S. Blues encore [28]
- Reviewer says the band was in high spirits throughout this tour [29]
- Reviewer says Deal had no second jam until late 1980, rebutting an earlier commenter [20]
- Reviewer calls this one of the hottest shows of 1989 and points to the Truckin' Up to Buffalo DVD [21]
- Reviewer found this show more powerful than the 1986 Rich Stadium show, which seemed weak to them [23]
- Reviewer finds it a mediocre late-80s show, paling beside many shows from around this period [26]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1989-07-04.118538.aud-matrix.pzm-dak5245.flac16**: taped by Robert Mullen; source: Equipment/Lineage: 2 DAK 5245 Microphones and 2 Realistic PZM Mics(Mounted on 1'x 1'x 3/8" plexiglass)>Realistic 4 Channel Mixer>Sony D6C Portable Stereo… [1]. Also: This is an audience matrix recording using PZM and DAK 5245 gear [1]
- **gd1989-07-04.akg414s.alexander.78771.flac16**: taped by Tim Alexander; transferred by Bill Tetzeli; source: FOB (AKG 414s) > Sony D-5 (Dolby B) [2]. Also: Reviewer notes the show has had an official CD/DVD release; Alexander's AKG 414 master had a tape flip about six minutes into Space [2][29]
- **gd1989-07-04.akg414s.alexander.78959.flac24**: taped by Tim Alexander; transferred by Bill Tetzeli; source: FOB (AKG 414s) > Sony D-5 (Dolby B) [3]. Also: Masters were lent by Tim Alexander; this is a 24-bit transfer with a tape flip in Space [3]
- **gd1989-07-04.166433.mtx.tobin.flac16**: transferred by Matrix by Kevin Tobin; source: SBD + AUD Matrix 2 Source Mix (44/16) [9]. Also: This is a mix made by an archive.org user, converted to FLAC in November 2023 [9]
- **gd89-07-04.aud.wiley.9045.sbeok.shnf**: source: AUD>MC>DAT>CDR [10]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Rich Stadium - July 4, 1989](https://www.dead.net/show/july-4-1989) [33]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Rich Stadium - July 4, 1989](https://www.dead.net/show/july-4-1989) [34]
